title: bhakti: the Chaitanya Charitamrita (selections)
hook: by a river, a renunciant asks a governor to teach him, and keeps saying: say more
tomorrow: what tears a garden of devotion up by the roots?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhakti that listens first: the stranger in the temple, and the scholar who turned. Today, a new week, and a conversation that keeps climbing.

Some conversations go deeper every time someone says: and? This one happens by the Godavari river, and the roles are upside down. Chaitanya is the renunciant, the one who left the world. Ramananda Raya is a governor, a householder, a man of the world. And it's the renunciant who asks the householder to teach. Ramananda hesitates. Chaitanya answers with a line the Charitamrita keeps: whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a teacher, whatever their birth, whether they've left home or not. So Ramananda begins. And every answer he gives gets the same reply.
screen: `BY THE GODAVARI RIVER.` → `THE RENUNCIANT ASKS TO BE TAUGHT.` → `EVERY ANSWER, THE SAME REPLY.`

segments.voice: Chaitanya asks: tell me the goal. Ramananda starts with duty: doing the work that's yours brings devotion to Vishnu. Chaitanya's reply becomes the refrain of the whole talk: that's on the outside; say more. Ramananda tries again. Offering the fruit of your work to Krishna. On the outside. Giving up your duties. Still outside. Devotion mixed with knowledge. Outside. Then Ramananda names a devotion that doesn't lean on knowledge at all, simple loving service. This time Chaitanya says: yes, that's so. Now go further. And the talk climbs. To prema, love itself. Then love for Krishna as a servant loves, then as a friend, then as a parent, then as a beloved. And at the top, Radha's love. That's why he keeps saying more. Bhakti here isn't one feeling. It's a ladder, and Chaitanya keeps asking for the next rung. Notice where the ladder starts. Duty and offered work, the heart of last week's karma, aren't thrown away; the talk calls them a first step. That's the Charitamrita's ladder, and Gaudiya Vaishnavas still teach from it; other Hindu schools order these paths their own way. And the book never forgets where it happened: a householder by a river, teaching the renunciant who asked.
screen: `THAT'S ON THE OUTSIDE. SAY MORE.` · `YES, THAT'S SO. GO FURTHER.` · `SERVANT, FRIEND, PARENT, BELOVED.` · then, large: `A LADDER, ONE RUNG FURTHER.`

segments.voice: If you can, stand and walk slowly across the room and back. With every few steps, let attention go one step further in: from the room, to your feet, to the breath, to the quiet under it. If you'd rather sit, take the same steps in your mind.
Bhakti: devotion, here a ladder. Every answer is good, and there's always a further rung.
Your line: bhakti, from the Chaitanya Charitamrita, one rung further. Day three of the book.

screen: `DAY 1660 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT TEARS UP THE GARDEN?`

original.note: Sanskrit prema, love; in Ramananda's answers, the rung after loving service, from which the ladder climbs to Radha's love.

trapdoor: what you thought: devotion is one feeling, the same all the way down.
what it means: in this talk bhakti is a ladder, from duty and offered work up through love as servant, friend, parent and beloved.

what a scholar hears: Chaitanya Charitamrita Madhya 8, the Ramananda samvada: varnashrama, karmarpana, svadharma-tyaga, jnana-mishra and jnana-shunya bhakti, prema, dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhurya, Radha's prema.
recall: the golden one, with Radha's heart

chat.meaning: By the Godavari, Chaitanya answers each good reply with 'go further': in this telling, bhakti is a ladder you keep climbing.

Godavari.meaning: a river in India, where this talk takes place

Ramananda Raya.meaning: a governor and devotee who teaches Chaitanya in the Charitamrita

Vishnu.meaning: the god who preserves the world; Krishna is honored as his form

Gaudiya Vaishnavas.meaning: devotees in the Krishna tradition that follows Chaitanya

sources.ref: Chaitanya Charitamrita, Madhya-lila 8 (the meeting with Ramananda Raya on the Godavari; whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a guru, whether brahmin, renunciant or shudra; the questions on the goal and the refrain 'this is external, say more'; devotion free of knowledge accepted, then prema, servitude, friendship, parental love, conjugal love, and Radha's love)

notes: Confirm the order of Ramananda's answers in Madhya 8 (varnashrama duty, offering the fruits of work, giving up duties, devotion mixed with knowledge, devotion free of knowledge, prema, then dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhurya, Radha's love) and where Chaitanya changes 'external' to 'this is so, go further'.
'Whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a teacher, whatever their birth' paraphrases Madhya 8.128 (brahmin, renunciant or shudra); confirm the softened wording.
'Other Hindu schools order these paths their own way' is general and unranked; confirm.
